one_month_reasoning: No company-scheduled catalyst falls inside 2026-09-30 to 2026-10-30: the fiscal Q4 FY26 report is expected in early-to-mid November (third-party calendars show Nov 4-11), after the window. Things that do fall in the window: peer/supply-chain reads (TSMC and other semi earnings in mid/late October, smartphone sell-through data), macro/rate prints, and any new data-center customer or Amazon tranche news, which could come at any time. Short-horizon technicals are mixed: a strong September rally (Amazon deal on Sep 8, Snapdragon Summit, Apple license renewal on Sep 24) peaked near $206 and then reversed, with a -7% day on Sep 28 that sources put down to profit-taking and a tech selloff. Reversal after a sharp move and momentum roughly cancel out. So I center on today's $184.5 with no drift and use a monthly sigma of about 14.5% (a bit under 54%/3.5 = 15.4%, because the 54% realized vol is inflated by the April-June spike from $122 to $260) and a lognormal spread.

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (60%: FY28 non-GAAP EPS est. $11.00 x 17x = $187) and FCF yield (40%: normalized FY28 FCF/share ~$10.70 at a 5.5% yield = $195), giving about $190 as the value the market should put on the stock by Sep 2027, when it will price off FY28 earnings.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: FY28 (Sep-2028 FY) non-GAAP EPS $11.00 x 17x forward P/E

inputs_detail.value: Data center ~$5B; non-handset growth >60% y/y (roughly +$7.5B), replacing ~all FY26 Apple product revenue; QCT Android revenue -20% y/y (>$1.50 EPS headwind); handset market down low teens

inputs_detail.derivation: Start from FY27 of about $9.3 (consensus; the Q4 run-rate of about $2.15 x 4 plus the data-center ramp less the Android drag). For FY28 add: part of the >$1.50 Android EPS headwind returning as memory normalizes (+$0.5); the data-center ramp from $5B toward $10B at mid-to-low GM with opex growing slower than revenue (+$0.8); gross margins recovering to 48-50% as double-digit price increases come in (+$0.3); a net share count of about -1%/yr after buybacks, Modular shares and the Amazon warrant (+$0.1). Total about $11.0. That is well below the straight-line path to management's >$18 FY29 target, which I haircut heavily because data-center execution is unproven.

The stock trades at about 19.8x NTM consensus ($184.5/$9.3) today. Handset-heavy QCOM has usually traded around 12-17x. I pick 17x: a premium to the old range for the data-center/auto mix shift (non-handset >50% of QCT in FY27), but below today's multiple because consensus EPS keeps getting cut (from $9.80 to $9.30 in 3 months) and the Street is mostly Hold (22 of 37).

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: Normalized FY28 FCF ~$11.4B / ~1,065M diluted shares = ~$10.70/share, capitalized at a 5.5% FCF yield

inputs_detail.value: $8,405M / $1,578M (includes $5,550M tax payments in excess of provision)
1,069M (Q3 FY26); +17.8M Modular shares issued; Amazon warrant for up to 25M shares at $161.26 (3.75M vested)
$20.56B remaining authorization; Q3 buyback avg price $222

inputs_detail.derivation: Add back the one-off tax cash outflow (~$4B above the normal level) to the 9M FY26 OCF to get about $12.5B of annualized normalized OCF. Grow it with FY28 EPS (~+15% from the FY26 level), then subtract higher capex (~$2.2B/yr, as data-center build-out lifted 9M capex to $1.6B from $0.8B). Result: about $11.4B.
Management's own buybacks at an average $222 imply they see FCF yields in the mid-single digits as attractive. The Street's Hold skew argues against a yield much below 5%. 5.5% sits between those.

bear.story: The memory-driven handset slump runs through FY27, Android revenue falls more than 20%, the Apple product exit is complete, and price increases fail to restore QCT gross margin. The ASIC ramp stays low-margin and the HBC accelerator slips past mid-2027 with no merchant wins beyond the two hyperscalers. FY28 EPS comes in around $8.5 and the multiple falls back to about 14x, the old handset-company level. That is roughly the April 2026 low ($122).

base.story: Data center hits about $5B in FY27, auto runs above a $7B annual rate, handsets bottom and recover modestly, and margins get back to the 48-50% GM range by mid-FY27. FY28 EPS comes in around $11 at 17-18x.

bull.story: The Amazon collaboration scales (more warrant tranches vest as purchases build toward $60B over 10 years), HBC silicon wins a third data-center customer, and the path to $15B data center / >$18 FY29 EPS becomes credible. FY28 EPS is around $12.5 at a 23x AI-infrastructure multiple, back toward the May 2026 peak ($260).

thesis_break_reason: Below about $130 (-30%), the stock would be pricing roughly 14x an EPS well under $9.3, i.e. the old handset-only multiple with no credit for data center. That most likely means something fundamental broke: the December-quarter ASIC revenue or the ~$5B FY27 data-center target slips, gross margins stay below range despite price increases, or the Android/China handset bottom that management called for the June quarter fails. Ordinary volatility at 45-54% vol can reach $150, so the break level sits below that.

reasoning: Primary-document read: the Q3 FY26 release and 10-Q show revenue of $9.9B (-4%) and non-GAAP EPS of $2.21 (-20%), with handsets -20% and auto +61%. The Q4 guide is $9.7-10.5B and $2.05-2.25 EPS, with QCT EBT margin down to 23-25%. On the official LSEG call transcript, management gave the key FY27 bridge: non-handset +60% (incl. ~$5B data center, first revenue in the December quarter from two hyperscaler ASICs with POs in hand) replaces roughly $7.5B of FY26 Apple revenue; Apple revenue falls ~50% sequentially into December; the handset market is down low teens with QCT Android -20% (>$1.50 EPS); price increases are double-digit and phase in over several quarters; custom data-center products drag GM by 1.5-2pt. The 8-Ks add what recaps skip: the Amazon warrant (25M shares at $161.26, only 3.75M vested, vesting tied to up to $60B of purchases), Modular paid with 17.8M new shares, and the 10-Q shows Q3 buybacks at an average $222 with $20.6B of authorization left. At the Goldman conference (Sep 8) the CFO reiterated $5B FY27 data center with 'very high confidence', a 30% operating margin within three years, and opex growing slower than revenue. The Apple license renewal (effective Apr 2027) removes a QTL tail risk. Consensus NTM EPS has been cut to about $9.30, so the stock is about 20x forward, which already credits the AI pivot. My FY28 EPS of about $11 at 17x plus an FCF-yield cross-check gives a fair value of about $190, near spot, i.e. no strong edge. I centered the 12-month distribution at a median of about $190 with lognormal sigma about 0.44 (below the 54% realized, which is inflated by the April-June spike, but well above a typical large cap's ±25-35%), and fattened the left tail slightly for the bear case (handset slump plus data-center slip, $120). Scenario mean is about $200 (0.25x120 + 0.5x192 + 0.25x290), consistent with the ladder. Research was limited to about 12 searches/fetches; Twelve Data estimates/targets were paywalled and Alpha Vantage was rate-limited, so consensus comes from a TIKR/Yahoo article.
